summary: Adds apparent thickness to line strips, triangles, or quads by copying geometry at a separation distance, optionally tapering or insetting it, and creating side quads.

key_params.name: axis
key_params.note: Extrude along normal, X, Y, or Z

key_params.name: peredge
key_params.note: Extrude faces as a group instead of individually

key_params.name: maxprimsperpoint
key_params.note: Temporary allocation limit when keeping faces connected

key_params.name: normal
key_params.note: Generate no, point, or vertex normals

key_params.name: cpureadback
key_params.note: Copy topology information back to the CPU

key_params.name: map
key_params.note: Map attributes to distance or taper

key_params.name: map0op
key_params.note: Map operation for the first mapping block

key_params.name: map0element
key_params.note: Source element for the first mapping block

key_params.name: map0parm
key_params.note: Target parameter for the first mapping block

key_concepts: Extrude POP gives line strips, triangles, or quads apparent thickness by offsetting copied geometry and creating side quads.
Axis, distance, taper, and per-edge settings decide whether faces extrude individually or as connected groups.
The Map page can vary distance or taper per point, while normal and CPU-readback controls prepare the result for shading and diagnostics.
common_gotchas: The docs recommend passing extruded output through Normal POP for faceted shading.
Mapped distance attributes can vary extrusion per point, so validate bounds and face connectivity.
Keep Faces Connected requires enough temporary storage for max primitives per point.
